owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to the contract's branch.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.
Never bypass guards: no --no-verify, no bypass env vars, no skip flags.
Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to the contract's branch as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.

tasks.title: One claims checker
requirements: scripts/gate/claims.mjs reads the status table of SR-5.04 (docs/status.json, or the path given by --status) and scans the files given by --surfaces (globs) for each feature's claim phrases; a feature whose row is planned and appears without the planned label, or a performance figure without a results file named in its row, is a finding
a planned row without a date older than four weeks is a warning and older than eight weeks is a finding that says give it a date, drop it, or move it to the roadmap (principle 5)
--json prints {features, claims, findings, warnings}; exit 1 on any finding; no dependencies; a version: comment on the first line

claims.mjs exits 2, distinct from 1 for a finding, and prints the cause when the status file is missing, is not valid JSON, has no feature rows, holds a status outside the documented set, or has no claim phrases, and when a --surfaces glob matches no file; --json reports the number of files scanned under the key files

claims.mjs and every file it imports only read files: they spawn no process, open no network connection, resolve no name, write nothing, and import only node:fs, node:path, node:url, node:process and ./ files under scripts/gate/ that obey the same rule; none uses createRequire, require(, process.binding, process.dlopen, process.getBuiltinModule, fetch, Reflect.get on globalThis, eval, Function, WebSocket, EventSource, globalThis[ or import(, nor any node:fs call that writes (writeFile, appendFile, createWriteStream, mkdir, rm, rename, copyFile, in their sync, callback and promise forms)

a planned feature counts as labelled only when the label sits in the same sentence as its claim phrase, inside the same block element (a paragraph, a list item, a table cell, a heading, a definition or a blockquote line), and in the same clause: within a sentence, clauses are split at ';' and at a comma or a dash followed by but, while, whereas or with, and a label covers only the phrases of its own clause; a common ancestor such as div, section, main or body is not the same element; each Markdown list item, table row and HTML li, tr and td is its own unit whatever its punctuation, and a label in one does not cover another; the label is the whole word planned ('unplanned' is not the label), and 'not planned', 'was planned', 'as planned' and 'no longer planned' are not the label; there are two exceptions to the same-element rule: an element of class tag whose whole text is the label labels the next sibling element only (the site's section tag), and a heading whose text ends with the label, as '(planned)' or ': planned', labels every unit of its section up to the next heading of the same or higher level; a heading that only uses the word ('What is built and what is planned'), a banner or any other page-wide line labels nothing; phrases match without regard to case, across line wraps, with HTML tags stripped, entities decoded, Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed (the link text kept), Unicode hyphens folded to '-' and typographic apostrophes and quotes folded to ASCII

a performance figure is a number, with thousands separators or a k suffix allowed, followed by a unit of time, throughput or size (ms, µs, s, seconds, minutes, MB, GB, TB, MB/s, ops/s, req/s, x or × faster, times faster, x or × less), with or without a space before the unit, or a percentage stated as a gain or a saving (40% fewer, 40% faster, 40% less), in a sentence; it needs a results file named in the row of the feature the sentence names, which must be a relative path to a .json file under a directory named results inside the checkout (this repository keeps its bench results under bench/results/) that parses to a non-empty object; a row whose results field names a directory, an absolute path, a path holding '..', a file that is not JSON, a file outside a results directory (docs/status.json itself included) or an empty JSON file makes claims.mjs exit 2 naming the row, and a figure sentence that names no feature is a finding; version numbers, durations such as a 14-day trial, prices and counts are not figures; a sentence carrying the marker <!-- claims: not a figure --> is exempt from this rule only
the age of a planned row comes from a field in the row (the date it was marked planned), never from a file time or git history; claims.mjs takes --now so tests fix the clock
the fixtures follow SR-5.04's status table as merged, and the CLI is tested end to end on fixtures at fixed paths

a planned row whose 'marked planned' field is missing, not an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or after --now makes claims.mjs exit 2 naming the row; a planned row whose target date is before --now is a finding naming the row, whatever its age

a --surfaces file of any other type (.mdx, .astro, .txt and so on) is scanned as plain text with HTML tags stripped, never skipped; with no --surfaces, claims.mjs scans README.md, **/*.md and **/*.html under the working directory, leaving out node_modules/ and .git/, and --json says which globs it used
when one row's phrase lies inside another row's phrase at the same place, only the longer phrase counts there

phrases from the status table are folded the same way as page text (case, Unicode hyphens, typographic apostrophes and quotes) and matched as literal text, never as a regular expression; a planned row with no non-empty phrase makes claims.mjs exit 2 naming the row
the text of the content attribute of a meta description, og:description or twitter:description tag, and of every alt, title and aria-label attribute, is scanned as a unit of its own

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/gate-claims.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest
